desc:
A warehouse log lists stock changes as [time, change]: a positive change is a delivery, a negative one is a pickup. The entries are in no particular order.

All changes that carry the same time happen together, so only their total counts at that moment. The stock level must never drop below zero after any moment has been applied.

Return the smallest non-negative initial stock for which this holds.

events = [[5, -3], [1, 2], [5, 2], [3, -4]]  ->  3

Sorted by time the totals are +2 at time 1, -4 at time 3 and -1 at time 5. Starting with 3, the stock goes 5, 1, 0 and never gets negative; starting with 2 it would reach -1.
constraints: Several events may share the same time
hints: The order of the entries in the input does not matter, but the order of the times does. What should you do first with the list?
After sorting by time and adding up the changes of equal times, you get a running balance. The initial stock only shifts that whole balance up.
If the lowest running balance (starting from 0) is m and it is negative, you need exactly -m units at the start; if it never goes below 0 the answer is 0.
editorial: Let b be the running total of changes after each distinct time, starting from zero. With an initial stock s the actual stock is s + b, which must stay non-negative everywhere. That is the case exactly when s ≥ -min(b), so the answer is max(0, -min(b)).

Grouping equal times matters: a pickup and a delivery at the same moment cancel, and only the net effect is checked. Sort the events by time (or collect the totals in a map and sort its keys), sweep once, and track the minimum balance. O(n log n) time, O(n) space.
